correctness.rationale: For every odd s>=3, the identity F_s=s integral_0^1 (tx+(1-t)y)^{s-1}dt proves convexity and compactness. Symmetry forces the nearest B_s point to (1,1) to lie on the diagonal at a=s^{-1/(s-1)}, giving the inward square-corner excess sqrt(2)(1-a). Convexity of distance-to-B_s bounds the square-to-body directed excess at that value. For xy<0, F_s=(u^s+v^s)/(u+v) bounds the sole coordinate exceeding the square by 2^{1/(s-1)}-1; a strictly concave scalar comparison on [0,1/2] shows this is smaller than the diagonal excess. Homogeneous Phi_p=F_p, Phi_2p=F_p(x,-y) and Phi_{2^k}=x^{2^{k-1}}+y^{2^{k-1}} then yield precisely the three claimed convex families, including p=3,k=2 boundaries; expansion 1-e^{-u} yields the asymptotic constants. The analytic inequality, not the script grid, supports all odd s.
